samples.summary: New Remove-link toolbar button (showRemoveLink) has no test at all, though it is now the only way to drop a hyperlink in Slides
samples.evidence: The diff adds a `showRemoveLink` prop, an `IconUnlink` ToolbarButton (aria-label "Remove link") and a `handleRemoveLink` callback in text-format-group.tsx, and opts it in from `text-edit-section.tsx` and `mobile-toolbar.tsx`. No test asserts (a) the button renders only when `showRemoveLink` is passed, (b) clicking it calls `editor.removeLink()` and re-focuses. `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts` already provides exactly the needed jsdom + createRoot + `[aria-label=...]` harness for TextFormatGroup, so such a test was cheap; `tests/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.test.ts` only does state-machine checks plus a module-import smoke test (`expect(typeof mod.TextEditSection).toBe("function")`) and merely stubs `removeLink: () => {}`. Since Clear formatting no longer removes hyperlinks (#1051) and slides has no link popover, a silently unrendered or unwired button leaves users with no way to remove a link, and nothing in CI would catch it (frontend has no tsc, and JSX props like a typo'd/never-passed flag fail silently).

samples.summary: 'removeLink still drops the hyperlink' asserts only a negative over an array it never pins down — passes even if the text (or all inlines) vanished
samples.evidence: The whole assertion is `expect(inlines.every((i) => !i.style.href)).toBe(true)`. `Array.every` is vacuously true on an empty array, so the test passes if `commitBlocks()[0].inlines` were empty, and it never asserts the link text survived (`removeLink` is supposed to keep the text and drop only the href — the sibling test asserts text via `inlines.map(i=>i.text).join('')`, this one does not). It also cannot distinguish `removeLink` working from `clearInlineFormatting` (called on the line before) having stripped the href — i.e. the very regression #1051 fixes would still make this test green.

samples.summary: 'removeLink is still how a hyperlink is dropped' cannot fail for the reason it names: it passes if clearInlineFormatting removed the href instead
samples.evidence: The test calls `editor.clearInlineFormatting()` and then `editor.removeLink()`, and asserts only `inline.style.href` falsy on every inline. If Clear formatting regressed back to stripping `href` (the pre-#1051 behavior these tests exist to guard), the assertion still holds, so the test does not attribute the removal to `removeLink`. It also does not assert the text or block structure survived `removeLink`. Making the assertion meaningful needs a positive check before `removeLink` (href present after clearing) or dropping the clear call.

samples.summary: The relocated isAtLinkTrailingEdge changed getBlock→findBlock to reach headers/footers/table cells, but no test exercises a caret in those containers
samples.evidence: The extracted helper deliberately swaps `this.doc.getBlock(...)` (throwing, caught → false) for `doc.findBlock(position.blockId)` with the comment that a caret in a header, footer or table cell now resolves. Every new test drives a plain top-level paragraph: `link-trailing-edge.test.ts` mounts `createEmptyBlock()` and types/inserts in block 0; `editor-clear-formatting.test.ts` uses a single 'paragraph' block; `text-box-clear-formatting.test.ts` uses a text box with no tables/headers. So the widened reach (the one behavioural difference of the extraction) is untested — a caret at a link edge inside a table cell or header could regress unnoticed.
searchedFor: Grep isAtLinkTrailingEdge across packages/docs (only src hits, no test hits)

samples.summary: The `prev.href === undefined` half of the exitsLink condition is never independently tested in either entry point
samples.evidence: Both new clear-formatting paths compute `exitsLink = isAtLinkTrailingEdge(...) || !!(prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined)` (text-editor.ts ~3441 and editor.ts ~3366). In every new test (`Cmd+\ at a link trailing edge still exits the link`, `the Clear formatting button at a link trailing edge also exits the link`) the caret is at the trailing edge, so the first disjunct already fires and the pending-state re-check is short-circuited. A scenario where pending carries `href: undefined` but the caret no longer reports a trailing edge (the case the comment says the re-check exists for) has no coverage, so that clause could be wrong or dead without any test failing.
searchedFor: read link-trailing-edge.test.ts (all new Cmd+\ / button cases)

samples.summary: The Cmd+\ key-set drift fix is only covered on the range path; no test shows the collapsed-caret shortcut now pends fontSize/fontFamily/color/backgroundColor
samples.evidence: The docstring states the shortcut previously omitted `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `color` and `backgroundColor` and now shares `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`. `editor-clear-formatting.test.ts` 'the Mod+\ shortcut keeps the hyperlink too' checks `color` falsy but only with a *range* selection (`selectWholeBlock`), which goes through `applyStyleToSelection`. The collapsed-caret branch (`this.pending?.set(CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, ...)`) is only exercised by the link tests in `link-trailing-edge.test.ts`, which assert nothing but `href` and text. So 'typing after Cmd+\ at a caret in a coloured/sized run produces a plain run' — the other half of the drift fix — is untested.

finding.summary: New Remove-link toolbar button (showRemoveLink) has no test at all, though it is now the only way to drop a hyperlink in Slides
finding.evidence: The diff adds a `showRemoveLink` prop, an `IconUnlink` ToolbarButton (aria-label "Remove link") and a `handleRemoveLink` callback in text-format-group.tsx, and opts it in from `text-edit-section.tsx` and `mobile-toolbar.tsx`. No test asserts (a) the button renders only when `showRemoveLink` is passed, (b) clicking it calls `editor.removeLink()` and re-focuses. `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts` already provides exactly the needed jsdom + createRoot + `[aria-label=...]` harness for TextFormatGroup, so such a test was cheap; `tests/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.test.ts` only does state-machine checks plus a module-import smoke test (`expect(typeof mod.TextEditSection).toBe("function")`) and merely stubs `removeLink: () => {}`. Since Clear formatting no longer removes hyperlinks (#1051) and slides has no link popover, a silently unrendered or unwired button leaves users with no way to remove a link, and nothing in CI would catch it (frontend has no tsc, and JSX props like a typo'd/never-passed flag fail silently).

verdict.reason: Verified the Remove-link button exists in text-format-group.tsx (prop `showRemoveLink` line 72/102, `aria-label="Remove link"` ToolbarButton lines 310-325, `handleRemoveLink` calling `editor.removeLink?.()` + `editor.focus()` lines 174-178), opted in by text-edit-section.tsx:93 and mobile-toolbar.tsx:580. Searched repo-wide for a counterexample test and found none: grep of `Remove link|showRemoveLink` over the whole repo (minus node_modules) yields zero test-file hits; `removeLink` in packages/frontend/tests appears only as inert stubs (mobile-text-toggles.test.ts:71 vi.fn never asserted, text-edit-section.test.ts:37 no-op stub, docs-link-popover.test.tsx:26 which tests a different Docs component). I read toolbar-focus.test.ts in full — it is the TextFormatGroup jsdom harness and explicitly covers showStrikethrough/showHighlight and Insert link, but never showRemoveLink or the "Remove link" label. No e2e directory exists; the only other mention of these labels is the exploratory script packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-dom.mjs, not an assertion. Editor-layer removeLink tests in packages/slides/docs cannot catch an unrendered/unwired toolbar button. Gap is real and, since Slides has no link popover, an untested regression would leave users no way to remove a hyperlink — major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: Text-box `clearInlineFormatting` collapsed-caret-at-link-trailing-edge case is untested (and lacks the override the docs path got)
finding.evidence: `TextBoxEditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` still calls `applyStyleImpl(CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE)` with no trailing-edge `href: undefined` override — the addition the diff made only to `EditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` (editor.ts:3366) and `TextEditor.clearFormatting`. The new test file `packages/docs/test/view/text-box-clear-formatting.test.ts` only covers a select-all range clear and `removeLink`; it never places a collapsed caret at a link's trailing edge, clears, and types. The docs counterpart deems exactly that scenario a defect ('the next typed character would silently extend the link') and covers it in link-trailing-edge.test.ts, but the slides/text-box equivalent (`text-box-link-trailing-edge.test.ts` covers only Space/Enter) has no such case, so link extension via the Slides Clear-formatting button ships with no coverage.

verdict.reason: The behavior the finding says is untested does not exist in the text-box path, so no defect can ship undetected through it. `TextBoxEditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` (text-box-editor.ts:1077-1082) routes to `applyStyleImpl`, which early-returns when there is no selection (text-box-editor.ts:819-820) and has no collapsed-caret `pending.set` branch anywhere (the only pending writes are stepSelectionFontSize at :884 and typing/paste merges at :982-1003). The docs defect mechanism is specifically `pending.set({...caretStyle, ...style})` re-seeding the link's href (editor.ts:3344-3372); with no pending write, the Slides button at a collapsed caret cannot re-arm or extend a link — it is simply a no-op, and packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:623-624 delegates straight to it. The keyboard half that DOES set pending inside a text box is the shared `TextEditor.clearFormatting` (text-editor.ts:3426-3448, pending wired at text-box-editor.ts:708), and that exact collapsed-caret-at-trailing-edge-then-type case is covered at link-trailing-edge.test.ts:236-250. The only residual is a parity gap (Slides button no-ops at a caret), which is a correctness/design question about non-test code and whose failure mode is "nothing happens", not link corruption — not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.
